item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded:
Personally, I found this one fairly underwhelming. I'd even go so far as to say disappointing.

The line between horror and…not, basically, is always a pretty fine line to run, especially when you're trying to play the unrevealed horror. You've got to give enough to make people genuinely concerned for their well-being while keeping enough mystery to leave them wondering, and let their imagination fill in the blanks for how bad it could REALLY be.

This one feels like it just kind of tripped and fell all over that line - it gives too much to be a full-scale "Oh god what is going on in there" feeling, but not nearly enough to put somebody in the position of feeling like one of the agents in a "Boots on the ground" gritty and personal style. And frankly, the added logs just kind of made it worse for me, especially the final log.

Log1
– hide block

The first log's issues have been gone over pretty noticeably, so in brief, the poor formatting in Team 1's communications is just annoying and a minor editing issue, and it does seem a little weird how the Foundation just kind of randomly throws trained agents into the woodchipper here. Also, Team 4's existence is poorly handled and pointless, and even mentioning them is pointless since they never interact with anything. Chekhov's Gun these guys.

Tale
– hide block

Trying to be fair, maybe I'd already hit enough bias to set me against it, but I'm pretty lukewarm on this tale for the same reasons as the rest of this SCP. There's zero information provided, and it just comes across as random "Hey this is awful isn't this awful?". No connection, no impact.

Log 2(3?)
– hide block

This one really put a final nail in the coffin.

Firstly, there is ZERO progress or new information from the first log. Nothing new is revealed, introduced, explained, or anything. It's basically a repeat of Log 1. Boring, redundant, and makes me LESS empathetic for the poor sods inside.

Secondly, the relationships between the agents sent in makes zero sense. Sir K is never established as field leader, which makes a NORMAL AGENT trying to supercede and ignore the decisions of an MTF SPECIALIST completely nonsensical. Even if we DO assume that K is in command, there are two FURTHER issues with this exchange. One - any decent field commander is going to want to take advantage of the specialist troops they've been given EXPLICITLY for this type of situation. That's just basic tactics. Two - again, ASSUMING we're going to run with K just steamrolling over the advice of the specialists, the attitude with which it's done is so incredibly abrasive and stupid that I'd almost think K is the SCP luring the rest of the team in, and that would actually be a better SCP.

Secondly(or Thirdly, for those keeping track), it really kind of upsets me that the Mole Rats here are being shown as such chumps. MTF agents are supposed to be elite, specialists, the best trained and equipped for their particular fields and types of situations, and these Rats are - effectively - D-class as far as how effective or competent they seem to be. This one is pretty much entirely a personal objection, but I really don't like the MTF agents just kinda getting crapped on without even being shown to be able to perform like they know what they're doing.

Sorry for getting a little wall-of-texty. >.>;

So if I was one of those guys that work for the SCPF who has to keep track of potentially dangerous SCP mixing/interactions, one that would greatly concern me would be if SCP-2467 attempted to assimilate SCP-455. This is not because it might take apart SCP-455, but if it left with even a fraction of SCP-455's ability to create weird internal spaces, because unlike SCP-455, SCP-2467 is mobile, and roaming the oceans. As such, I am proposing the following addendum:

Addendum: Due to the potential of SCP-2467 finding and possibly attempting to assimilate SCP-455, and the consequences of such an event, procedures to prevent such an interaction are currently being reviewed. In addition, contingency plans for such a containment breach are also being reviewed.

I dont like this. It fucks with your head then kills you. Isnt that effectively one that kills you?

I wish I had more to say, the main article is so anemic that the supplementary documents just end up treading water (no pun intended) in the sea of confused encounters and time problems.

But its like all the 'unnerving' tricks have been put together randomly in an article:

Yeah this thing can straight up kill you whenever it wants and no-one knows what happens to you. Vague, samey, boring.
Time changes, so you cant guarantee ho long you'll be in there for, wooooo!!! If it kills you why does it matter?
What does it do exactly? It throws out all of these seemingly random effects with no linking narrative.

I think that this SCP mildly effects the mind, all it does is make people forget where they are and make them want to wander inside. So to me this SCP is just as bad as getting lost in the supermarket when you're a child. Pretty terrifying but its over quickly.

item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded: I don't see anything wrong with the "perfect" conversion to feet. If I were a scip and exactly 6'5" tall, with the documentation procedures the Foundation uses calling for metric being the primary system used, there would be a funky decimal in the metric measurement, but 6'5" would still be the Imperial measurement. The Imperial measurements aren't always included in an article, but if you consider that an Agent reading the file for any given scip could be in/from a place where Imperial units are the norm, it helps said Agent visualize the scale of whatever more easily. This one is a little different because it's a wonky spaces distorting thing, but something could have been built using Imperial, so metric measurements don't look as "pretty". Instead of "how big is 182.88 meters?" they think, "ahh, two football fields. Got it."

item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded:
I really like this one. i've got to admit I'm a sucker for "bigger on the inside" stuff and incomprehensible buildings so this really strikes a chord with me. Both the main article and the logs are very well written too and just make me want to learn more about this thing, although I'm glad none of them go in too much detail so it keeps you speculating.

With that said, I do have a few nitpicks about things I feel could be improved and would make this SCP even better:

Main article
– hide block

Internal structure appears to be a random assembly of rooms, halls, and structures.

This sentence is a bit awkwardly worded, especially due to the repetition of the word "structure". I suggest the following replacement: "The internal configuration appears to be a random assembly of rooms, halls and miscellaneous structures".

a hall extending for 182.88 m (600 ft) Internal structure appears to be a random assembly of rooms, halls, and structures.

Hmmmm, direct translations from feet to metres. Never a good idea. It's the kind of detail that immediately breaks the immersion.

Experiment log
– hide block

I feel all transcripts should indicate who is speaking because the way it's currently formatted, it gets confusing quick (not to mention some of them do specify who's speaking, so why isn't it the case everywhere?).

I am also rather confused as to why Team 3 was not informed of the evac team's presence. I don't see what good hiding this from them is supposed to be; if anything, it's very counterproductive to have a rescue team if the other guys don't know they can ask them for help.

On top of that, considering how the previous exploration went, you really don't want the exploration team to be surprised by heavily armed people they weren't expecting raiding the place. This whole thing just seems to be begging for a disaster.

Oh and one more thing, it really shouldn't be called "experiment log" since they aren't actually conducting any experiments. It's just as much of an exploration log as the second one.

Exploration log
– hide block

Following document contains the whole and entirety of Exploration Log Record 455

Hum, stop me if I'm wrong but I do believe "whole" and "entirety" mean the same thing.

K and S arguing just seems… out of place It's uncharacteristically unprofessional for SCP personel, and you'd think one of them would have been given a leader position so orders could not be discussed.
